s.t: A donkey carried heavy sacks for a miller.
s.fr: Un âne porta de lourds sacs pour un meunier.

s.t: The sacks were full of grain for the mill.
s.fr: Les sacs étaient pleins de grain pour le moulin.

s.t: The donkey carried the grain for many years.
s.fr: L’âne porta le grain pendant de nombreuses années.

s.t: But the donkey grew old and weak.
s.fr: Mais l’âne devint vieux et faible.

s.t: His legs grew weaker every day.
s.fr: Ses jambes devenaient plus faibles chaque jour.

s.t: He could no longer carry the heavy sacks.
s.fr: Il ne pouvait plus porter les lourds sacs.

paras.summary: A donkey carries heavy sacks of grain to the mill for a miller for many years, but he grows old and weak, his legs grow weaker every day, and he can no longer carry the heavy sacks.

s.t: The miller gave him no food now.
s.fr: Le meunier ne lui donnait plus de nourriture maintenant.

s.t: The miller planned to kill him.
s.fr: Le meunier planifiait de le tuer.

s.t: The donkey was afraid, and he left the mill that night.
s.fr: L’âne avait peur, et il quitta le moulin cette nuit-là.

paras.summary: The miller gives him no food now and plans to kill him, so the donkey is afraid and leaves that night.

s.t: There was a town named Bremen.
s.fr: Il y avait une ville nommée Bremen.

s.t: He thought he could still sing well.
s.fr: Il pensait qu’il pouvait encore chanter bien.

s.t: "I will go to Bremen," said the donkey.
s.fr: « J’irai à Bremen, » dit-il, l’âne.

s.t: "I will become a town musician there."
s.fr: « Je deviendrai un musicien de ville là-bas ».

paras.summary: There is a town named Bremen, and the donkey thinks he can still sing well, so he decides to go there and become a town musician.

s.t: A dog hunted with a hunter for many years.

s.t: The dog caught many animals for him.

s.t: But the dog grew old and slow.
s.fr: Mais le chien devint vieux et lent.

s.t: The old dog could not catch animals now.
s.fr: Le vieux chien ne pouvait pas attraper des animaux maintenant.

paras.summary: A dog hunts with a hunter for many years, running with him every day and catching many animals, but he grows old and slow and cannot catch animals now.

s.t: The hunter did not want an old dog.
s.fr: Le chasseur ne voulait pas un vieux chien.

s.t: But the dog wanted to stay.
s.fr: Mais le chien voulait rester.

s.t: The hunter planned to kill him.
s.fr: Le chasseur planifiait de le tuer.

s.t: The dog was afraid, so he left that night.
s.fr: Le chien avait peur, alors il partit cette nuit-là.

paras.summary: The hunter does not want an old dog, but the dog wants to stay, so the hunter plans to kill him, and the dog is afraid and leaves that night.

s.t: On the road, he met the old donkey.
s.fr: Sur la route, il rencontra le vieux âne.

s.t: "Why are you afraid?" asked the donkey.
s.fr: « Pourquoi avez-vous peur ? » demanda l’âne.

s.t: The dog told the donkey the plan.
s.fr: Le chien dit à l’âne le plan.

s.t: "Come to Bremen," said the donkey.
s.fr: « Viens à Brême, » dit l’âne.

s.t: "You can still bark loudly there."
s.fr: « Tu peux encore aboyer fort là-bas. »

s.t: The dog agreed, and they walked on together.

paras.summary: On the road, the dog meets the donkey, who asks why the dog is afraid; the dog tells him the plan, the donkey invites him to Bremen, saying he can still bark loudly there, and the dog agrees, and they walk on together.

s.t: The cat sat in the window of the house.

s.t: But the cat grew old in the woman's house.

s.t: The cat's teeth were old and dull now.

s.t: She could no longer catch the mice for the woman.

paras.summary: A cat catches mice for an old woman for many years, sitting in the window of the house, but she grows old, her teeth are old and dull now, and she can no longer catch the mice.

s.t: The woman did not want the old cat now.

s.t: The woman planned to drown the old cat.

s.t: The old cat was afraid, and she left that night.

paras.summary: The woman does not want the old cat now and plans to drown her, so the cat is afraid and leaves that night.

s.t: The cat told the donkey and the dog the plan.

s.t: "Come to Bremen with us," said the donkey.

s.t: "You can still sing well at night."
s.fr: « Tu peux encore bien chanter la nuit. »

s.t: The cat agreed, and they walked on together.
s.fr: La chatte accepta, et ils marchèrent ensemble.

paras.summary: On the road, she meets the donkey and the dog, who ask why she is afraid; she tells them the plan, the donkey invites her to Bremen, saying she can still sing well at night, and the cat agrees, and they walk on together.

s.t: A rooster lived on a farm for many years.
s.fr: Un coq vivait dans une ferme depuis de nombreuses années.

s.fr: Chaque matin, il chantait fort pour réveiller la ferme.

s.t: But the rooster grew old and tired.
s.fr: Mais le coq devint vieux et fatigué.

s.t: He did not crow loudly now.
s.fr: Il ne chantait plus fort maintenant.

s.t: No one on the farm wanted the old rooster now.
s.fr: Personne à la ferme ne voulait le vieux coq maintenant.

paras.summary: A rooster lives on a farm for many years, crowing loudly every morning to wake the farm, but he grows old and tired, does not crow loudly now, and no one on the farm wants him.

s.t: The farm had guests that day.
s.fr: La ferme avait des invités ce jour-là.

s.fr: Le cuisinier planifiait de cuisiner le vieux coq pour les invités.

s.t: The old rooster did not want to be cooked.

paras.summary: The farm has guests that day, and the cook plans to cook the old rooster for them, but he does not want to be cooked, so he is afraid and flies from the farm that night.

s.t: On the road, he met the three animals.

s.t: "You can still crow loudly there."

paras.summary: On the road, he meets the three animals, who ask why he is afraid, and the rooster tells them the cook's plan; the donkey invites him to Bremen, saying he can still crow loudly there, and the rooster agrees, so all four walk on together.

s.t: They stopped in a forest.

paras.summary: The four animals walk all day toward Bremen, but night comes before they reach the town, so they stop in a dark forest, where the donkey and the dog lie down by a tree.

s.t: The rooster flew to the top of the tree.

paras.summary: The four animals come to a small house with one light in the window, so they walk to look, and the donkey puts his front feet on the window and looks inside.

s.t: The table was full of food.
s.fr: La table était pleine de nourriture.

s.t: The donkey came down and told the others.
s.fr: L’âne descendit et dit aux autres.

paras.summary: The animals have had no food all day, wanting the food and the warm house, so the donkey says they must make the robbers run away.

s.t: The dog climbed onto the donkey's back.

s.t: The cat climbed onto the dog's back.

s.t: The rooster flew up on top of the cat.

paras.summary: The dog climbs onto the donkey's back, the cat climbs onto the dog's back, and the rooster flies up on top of the cat, and the four animals make the sound together.

s.t: The donkey brayed.

s.t: The dog barked.
s.fr: Le chien aboya.

s.t: The cat screeched.

s.t: The rooster crowed.

s.t: The four animals went inside.

paras.summary: The four animals come down from the window, walk to the door, and the donkey pushes it open so they can go inside.

s.fr: La table était encore pleine de nourriture.

s.t: The four animals ate and were full.

s.fr: L’âne retourna dehors dans la cour.

s.t: There, he lay down on straw.

s.t: The straw was warm.
s.fr: La paille était chaude.

paras.summary: The table is still full of food, and the four animals eat and are full; the donkey goes back out to the yard, where he lies down on warm straw.

s.fr: Le chien se coucha derrière la porte.

s.t: The cat lay down by the warm ashes.
s.fr: Le chat se coucha près des cendres chaudes.

s.t: The rooster flew up onto the roof.
s.fr: Le coq vola jusqu’au toit.

s.t: Soon, all four animals were asleep.
s.fr: Bientôt, les quatre animaux dormaient.

s.t: That night, they were warm, safe, and full.
s.fr: Cette nuit-là, ils étaient chauds, en sécurité et rassasiés.

paras.summary: The dog lies down behind the door, the cat lies down by the warm ashes, the rooster flies up onto the roof, and soon all four animals are asleep, warm, safe, and full that night.

s.t: But the house was dark and quiet.
s.fr: Mais la maison était sombre et silencieuse.

s.t: The house was warm now.

paras.summary: The robber runs out into the yard, where the donkey wakes and kicks him, and he falls down in the yard, his face and his leg still hurting, then stands up and runs away.

paras.summary: The rooster wakes on the roof and crows loudly into the night; the sound is strange to the robber, and he is more afraid of the house now, never wanting to go back.

paras.summary: The robber reaches the other robbers, tired and afraid, and the other robbers see his fear, so the chief asks why he is afraid.
